4865-79010.notes: RETRACTED - I reported that 417 classes across 103 files compiled to nothing and painted opaque. THAT WAS FALSE and the row is kept rather than deleted so the claim does not resurface. text-white/64 and opacity-44 DO compile in this project. The gate is real in Tailwind 3.4 - node_modules/tailwindcss/src/util/pluginUtils.js:160 returns undefined when theme.opacity has no such key, and the stock scale is multiples of five - but skai-ui's preset FILLS theme.opacity with every integer 0..100 at tailwind-preset.ts:387, committed in d416a1a, precisely to close that hole. Its own comment records the same evidence I rediscovered, including the 194 live call sites at the time. So the hole was found and fixed before this wave. MY INSTRUMENT WAS THE DEFECT: I compiled a probe sheet against a MINIMAL config, not tailwind.config.ts, after a grep for the literal string 'opacity: {' missed a scale built with Object.fromEntries. The sanity assertions I added asserted /5, /70 and opacity-40, which hold under BOTH the stock scale and the project's, so they could not tell the two apart. A sanity check made only of facts that the broken and the correct instrument both reproduce cannot discriminate between them - it has to assert something the suspected failure would change. Wave 8's text-white/70 to text-white/64 change was CORRECT and is not a regression. The 9 class edits I made in BetPanel and GameExitConfirm are equivalent CSS and were left in place; the oracle that asserted the false rule has been deleted.

Each array runs EDGE->CENTRE and getMultiplierSlotColor indexes it by distance from the centre bucket, so the row is symmetric exactly as all three frames draw it. The old getMultiplierSlotColors mapped t = index/(total-1) monotonically and colour-inverted the right half of every board; the comment asserting the frame was "NOT a symmetric center-out ramp" was itself the bug and is replaced - those nine stops were precisely the nine distinct colours of the mirrored HALF row. STILL PARTIAL, but only because of the three ball frames, which cannot be exercised on a 0-POINTS box. ★ DEFECT 1 - PLINKO WAS UNPLAYABLE ON A PHONE, and nobody had recorded it. PlinkoGame's widget body was `flex flex-row` at EVERY width while the bet panel is `shrink-0` at up to 356px, so at 375 the game area was left ~19px and, after its own px-4, the canvas MEASURED 0px WIDE - a player on a phone saw no board at all. 11530-303164.title: dropdown-tokens
11530-303164.notes: NODE DATA BOTH SIDES 2026-09-01, and this row was PARTIAL earlier in this lane on a leading I have since shown the code cannot be blamed for. GEOMETRY panel 200x160 gap8 pad8 r12 = width={200}; four rows 184x28 r4 pad6/8 gap8, each carrying a 16x16 glyph at x=8 with the label at x=32 - all matched. COLOUR matched: #122524 on #123F3C w1 INSIDE, DROP_SHADOW r12 0,4 #000000@0.24, #FFFFFF labels, row 0 washed #123F3C. TYPE the frame says Manrope Regular 12/14 ls-4pct and SocialMenu SIZE.sm ships text-[12px] leading-4 = 12/16; the ROW BOX is 28 either way here because the 16px glyph floors it. * THE 12/14 IS NOT A BREAKPOINT STEP AND NO CODE CHANGE FIXES IT. Reported by lane w10-social-profile, who owns SocialMenu.tsx, and RE-MEASURED HERE rather than taken on trust: dropdown-time 11530:302910 and 11530:302923 are BOTH 120 wide and differ only in leading (12/16 at boardX 6819, 12/14 at 11752), so the leading cannot be a function of frame width; and dropdown - tridots - reply assigns it the OTHER WAY ROUND - 11530:303366 is 200 wide at boardX 37398 and 12/16 while 11530:303337 is 200 wide at boardX 40187 and 12/14. So the file contains TWO full redraws of the same menu set with different leading, and at 200 wide it says both. SocialMenu SIZE.sm = 12/16 reproduces one of the two drawings exactly. A width-keyed third size would fix this frame by breaking its equally authoritative twin, which is why it is filed against the FRAME and not the code. * AND THE ROW-BOX RULE, corrected: it is 6 + max(lineHeight, 16 when the row carries a glyph) + 6, not 6 + lineHeight + 6. Measured across the mobile board - 12/14 with a glyph gives 28 (11530:303164, 11530:303236), 12/14 without one gives 26 (11530:303293), 12/16 without one gives 28 (11530:303287), 14/18 without one gives 30 (9646:214871). CORRECTING MYSELF: I first wrote that SocialRowMenus.figma.test.tsx:308 is missing the max() term and is therefore wrong on every menu in this family. IT IS NOT, and the reason is structural. ROW_BASE (SocialMenu.tsx:101-102) is `flex ... items-center ... py-1.5` and MenuGlyph (:335) renders a `flex size-4 shrink-0` span, so in a flex row with items-center the content box IS max(line box, 16) - flexbox applies the floor for free, and the frames' rule is already the rule the DOM follows. At both shipped sizes the max never binds: md is 6+max(18,16)+6=30 and sm is 6+max(16,16)+6=28, which is why the helper's leading+2*pad reproduces every frame in the family, glyph-bearing or not. The floor is a LATENT term, not a missing one. * AND THAT IS THE SECOND, INDEPENDENT REASON AN xs SIZE WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG: a sub-16 leading is exactly when the max starts binding, so an xs at 12/14 would compute 26 in code against the 28 every glyph-bearing frame draws - unsound on the DOM alone, before the twin-frame evidence is even reached. Credit to lane w10-social-profile, who read the source rather than the formula and corrected their own row too; verified here at SocialMenu.tsx:89-90, :101-102, :335 and at the helper's `return leading + 2 * pad`. Nothing to change in any of the three copies of the helper. So: the code is right, the frame set is self-contradictory, and per SCHEMA that is a frame-defect rather than an implementation verdict. Mount is live - see 9636-208873.

11442-164766.title: Skai > Social 1VH (375 x 812px)
11442-164766.notes: STATUS CONFIRMED, REASON REPLACED. The standing reason on this frame and ~34 siblings is "there is no post entity in the database". That is true of Postgres and FALSE of the system, so it has been pointing every reader at a schema design that is not the work. Measured 2026-09-01 against the live chain and the live indexer. THE POST ENTITY EXISTS AND IS ROUTED: SKAISocialFeed.sol:243 declares createPost(bytes32 contentHash, uint256 parentId) with struct Post at :93 and event PostCreated at :161; indexer/ingester/ingester.go:4633 builds sktypes.SocialPost and :4642 calls PutSocialPost; indexer/store/store.go:3069 persists it under prefixSocialPost; indexer/api/rest/server.go:781 routes GET /api/v1/social/feed, and https://indexer.skai.trade/api/v1/social/feed?limit=5 answers HTTP 200 {"success":true,"data":[],"pagination":{"total":0}}. THE ACTUAL BLOCKER IS A BRICKED PREDEPLOY SET: eth_getCode on 0x5B41...0090 / 0091 / 0092 / 0093 returns the SAME 55-byte word on all four, 0x7f360894a13ba1a3210667c828492db98dca3e2076cc3735a920a3ca505d382bbc545f365f5f855af43d5f5f3e6029573d5ff35b3d5ffd, and every eth_call reverts with "execution reverted: stack underflow (5 <=> 6)". The disassembly explains it exactly: PUSH32 slot, SLOAD, PUSH0, CALLDATASIZE, PUSH0, PUSH0, DUP6 - DUP6 needs six stack items and finds five, so the stub reverts on ANY calldata and the implementation it points at is irrelevant. The ERC-1967 slot 0x360894...382bbc reads 0x...1090 / 1091 / 1092 / 1093 respectively, and each of those four addresses ALSO holds the identical 55-byte stub. Controls on the same RPC in the same minute: sUSD 0x5B41...0002 holds 6207 bytes and decimals() answers 0x06; eth_blockNumber 0x6f3b0d. So the RPC is healthy and only the social set is dead. THE ITEM IS A REDEPLOY, NOT A SCHEMA DESIGN - and it is necessary but NOT sufficient: contentHash is a bytes32 IPFS CID with no uploader anywhere in src (src/components/social/post/storyMedia.ts:19-20 records the same absence), so a post body still has nowhere to live.

Forking Crash is the right move for the PANEL, the WRONG move for the engine, and - as of the g-shell lane - the wrong move for the PAGE CHROME too. The Crash surface is ~7,950 lines across five files (AviatorGamePro.tsx 5,167, crashLiveRoundService.ts 919, crashMultiplayerService.ts 490, CrashPageSections.tsx 1,111, crashPageContent.ts 262). ★ DO NOT COPY CrashPageSections FOR THE PAGE SCAFFOLD. The title row, fairness sub-bar, section rhythm, page column cap and footer are SHELL, shared by all eleven game pages, and they now exist as components: PlayGamePageShell, PlayGameTitleRow, PlayGameSection, PlayGameSectionDivider, PlayGameSubBarSurface, PlayGamePageFooter from @gaming/components/play/shared, with the measurements and frame ids documented in shared/playPageTemplate.ts. Building the chrome by hand reproduces a fix eleven times and re-imports this frame's reversed title row; it also walks into the two traps that have already caught shipped pages - the fairness sub-bar is 12px = `rounded-lg` (`rounded-xl` is 16px in this app, and nine of ten shipped page files got it wrong), and the title art square is `rounded-[6px]` NOT `rounded-md` (10px here). Reusable near-verbatim FROM CRASH: the entire bet panel including Manual/Auto tabs, 1/2 - 2X - Max chips, the Auto block and the On Win / On Loss / Increase By / Stop on Win / Stop on Loss ladder (Slide's 10030-42517 and 10117-46330 draw these identically to Crash's), the live-bets card, the history strip, and the shared-round lifecycle scaffolding in crashLiveRoundService (countdown, participants count, round open/close). Genuinely NEW and not forkable: the reel component itself - a clipped overflow strip, a deterministic easing curve that must land the correct card exactly under a fixed centre needle, the enlarge/highlight transition on the landing card, the edge fade mask, and the multiplier-to-colour tier scale; plus the server-side round engine (a per-round landing multiplier drawn from a declared distribution, provably-fair commit-reveal, and settlement). ROUGH SIZE: front end ~1.2-2k lines (the chrome is now shell components rather than a fork, the panel is a fork, and the reel is the only real front-end work), server ~400-700 lines, plus the registration tax every game pays - App.tsx route, Play.tsx tile, gameTypeNormalization entry, gameSettlementService type, a `site_config` max-bet row (see the 9-games-frozen-at-defaults finding), a daily-loss-cap row, and a feature flag. ★ THE ANIMATION IS A CORRECTNESS SURFACE, NOT A POLISH SURFACE: the reel must be driven BY the settled result, never the result read off where the animation stopped, or the display and the ledger will disagree exactly the way Crash's 100x display cap already does. ||| QUESTIONS THIS LANE RAISED - FOUR NOW ANSWERED, TWO STILL OPEN. ANSWERED 2026-08-19: (1) Target Multiplier or Auto Cashout - RULED Auto Cashout, and the labels collapse to the same rule anyway; the target is locked before the round and there is no mid-slide exit. (2) Landing distribution and house edge - Limbo's math at a 1% edge, anchored to _shared/limbo.ts:52, with targets bounded 1.01x..1000x by limbo.ts:45-46. (3) Are the reel cards a FIXED finite set or a continuous draw rendered as cards? - CONTINUOUS. Limbo's roll is a uniform integer over LIMBO_SCALE = 1e8 (limbo.ts:61-66), so the landing is drawn from a continuum and the twelve cards are a RENDERING of it, not a wheel the game is built from. This also disposes of the max-win-exposure worry in the old (6): exposure is bounded by LIMBO_MAX_TARGET_BPS = 1000x, because the payout is at the TARGET and the target is what is capped - the landed value can print higher without costing more. STILL OPEN AND WORTH CASEY'S TIME: (A) Shared round or per-player? "Participants: 128" and "everyone's watching the same slide" say shared, and that is materially more infrastructure than Limbo needs - limbo.ts is single-player and carries NO round identity, so the shared-round lifecycle (roundId, participant count, countdown, one landing broadcast to all) is the genuinely new server work and has no existing implementation to fork except Crash's. (B) Which currency rails at launch - the panels disagree between SKAI and USDC, and per the standing gates the sUSD relays and real-money play are separate decisions. NEITHER OF THESE BLOCKS THE REEL OR THE PANEL, so build can proceed ahead of them; (A) blocks the server round engine specifically. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-26 (was `not-started`): re-verified live against the Figma page, the route table and prod site_config.
